title: DEF CON 26 CTF Network Packet Capture (2018) and Extracted CIC-IDS-Style Flow Feature Vectors
description:
Dataset package for the DEF CON 26 CTF 2018 network capture and its extracted flow features, assembled for the Rust-CICFlow evaluation corpus.

The primary artifact is the full DEF CON 26 CTF packet capture: a single 52.92 GB pcapng file (49.0 GB of packet content + pcapng overhead per 16.3 KB mean block) containing 156,114,913 Ethernet packets (linktype 1, single interface, all Enhanced Packet Blocks) captured during the DEF CON 26 Capture-The-Flag competition (first packet 2018-08-10 22:48:42 UTC; TCP-dominated adversarial CTF traffic).

Because ingest-side reuse benefits from compact slices, three byte-exact representative subsets (200,000 packets each, raw block copies preserving SHB + IDB + contiguous EPBs) accompany the full capture:

  • defcon26_head.pcapng - packets [0, 200000): event start, scan/handshake-dominated (~129 B mean frame, 25.7 MB)
  • defcon26_mid.pcapng - packets [78,057,456, 78,257,456): event peak, bulk game traffic (~506 B mean frame, 101.3 MB)
  • defcon26_tail.pcapng - last 200,000 packets: event end (48.0 MB)

Extracted flow features. The 84-feature CIC-IDS/CICFlowMeter-style bidirectional flow vector was extracted with Rust-CICFlow (config: flow timeout 120 s flow-age, activity timeout 5 s, min-packets 2, canonical payload-based length accounting, sample variance per Welford). Full-capture run: 156,114,913 packets → 7,798,789 flows in ~700 s single-threaded (4,583.4 MB CSV), plus the six subset flow CSVs (Rust and Python reference extractor outputs for head/mid/tail) that document measured feature parity and its four traced upstream semantic deltas.

Verification. SHA-256 checksums for every file are provided in SHA256SUMS.txt. The stream is suitable for intrusion-detection benchmarking, adversarial traffic analysis, and extractor reproducibility experiments.

Provenance. The source packet histogram derives from the DEF CON 26 ctf packet captures archive published on media.defcon.org; the flow-feature extraction and the subset slicing tool (scripts/extract_subsets.py) were produced with the open-source Rust-CICFlow engine and harness in this repository. Attribution to DEF CON and to traffic-derived artifacts is embedded in the README; the Python-side pip reference is cicflowmeter 0.2.0 (uehara).
